subject: FinByte follow-up: compatibility handoff & sprint plan
summary: Post-demo follow-up where FinByte asked for an explicit compatibility test plan vs hyperscaler APIs (OpenAI-compatible surface). We agreed on a short sprint: SDK swap smoke tests, prompt-output diffs, latency/cost targets and a two-week POC. Next step: kickoff tech scoping call (Aditya + FinByte engs) and deliver compatibility matrix.
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel@finbyte.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <m.gomez@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up & a couple of asks from today's demo

Hi Irene —

Thanks for the demo this morning. The team liked the latency profile and the batching ideas you showed. Before we escalate to procurement we need a concrete compatibility plan: our product currently talks to OpenAI-compatible endpoints (openai.ChatCompletion.create + existing SDK flow). Two specific asks: 

1) A short list of migration tests that prove feature parity (chat calls, attachments/streams, function/tool calling).
2) A simple checklist for our infra team to swap the SDK with minimal code changes; we prefer examples in Node + Python.

If you can send a compact plan and proposed timeline, we can book an internal architecture review next week. We are tentatively budgeting for a mid-July POC if things look good.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director of Engineering — FinByte

Attachments: none
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@finbyte.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & a couple of asks from today's demo

Hi Daniel —

Really appreciate the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can prove compatibility and give you a low-friction SDK swap path. I attached a draft compatibility matrix and a concise migration checklist (see attachments). High-level proposal: 

- Week 1 (this week): technical scoping call to confirm exact OpenAI API surfaces you use (Aditya + your engs).
- Week 2: SDK swap smoke tests (Node + Python) run by your team with our support; we'll provide example snippets and a small shim if needed.
- Week 3: prompt-output diffs and edge-case tests (function calling, streaming, tokenization/stop sequences).
- Week 4: POC run with production-like traffic for latency & cost validation.

Deliverables we'll share by end of day Thursday: compatibility-matrix.xlsx (mapping endpoints & behaviors), migration-checklist.md, and sample SDK snippets. Proposed prep call: Thursday 10am PT — does that work for you?

Notes: We recommend starting with your least risky routes (bulk ingestion/embeddings or non-real-time chat flows) to validate batching and KV cache behavior before switching high-SLA endpoints.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: compatibility-matrix.xlsx, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-checklist.pdf
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@finbyte.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & a couple of asks from today's demo

Daniel —

Adding a couple of technical clarifications ahead of the scoping call: 

- SDK swap: our Node and Python snippets are small wrappers around standard OpenAI-like calls. Typical change surface is ~2-4 lines for initialization and request/response handling if you use the standard client. We'll share diff examples.
- Function calling: behavior is compatible but we do surface deterministic differences around JSON schema validation and null/undefined handling; we'll include a small test harness that runs your function-calling test cases and highlights diffs.
- Streaming: we support chunked streaming compatible with EventSource/Server-Sent-Events. If you rely on incremental token-level side-effects, we'll test for reassembly differences.
- Tokenization: if you have custom stop-sequence logic, include a representative prompt set; small tokenization differences can shift costs — we'll quantify cost delta on your sample traffic during the POC.

Irene — I can run the initial smoke tests with their engs on Thursday if the 10am PT slot is confirmed.

— Aditya
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@finbyte.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & a couple of asks from today's demo

Daniel / team —

Thanks for the quick responses and for lining up the scoping call. Confirming next steps and owners: 

1) Tech scoping call — Thursday 10:00am PT (Irene + Aditya + FinByte engs). Owner: Irene to send calendar invite and agenda.
2) Deliverables by end of day Thursday: compatibility-matrix.xlsx (Irene), migration-checklist.md (Irene), Node/Python snippets (Aditya).
3) Smoke tests — Week 2: run by FinByte with Redwood on call. Owner: Aditya. Criteria: successful end-to-end chat, streaming session, and function-call sample without major schema regressions.
4) Prompt-output diffs & cost/latency report — Week 3: Redwood to deliver comparative report vs current hyperscaler baseline. Owner: Redwood Research/Applied ML (Aditya).
5) Two-week POC target window — mid-July. Owner: FinByte + Redwood CS contact (we'll assign once contract stage is confirmed).

If any of these feel off, flag them now. Otherwise Irene, please share the invite + the two attachments and the short checklist. We'll join the scoping call ready to run tests.

Ben Carter
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
